text.p: Israeli bonds closed down on Wednesday with CPI-linked bond prices falling on expectations of a low September consumer price index (CPI), traders said.
* Consumer price index (CPI) linked government bonds: -0.2 pct to 168.11
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon - issued for four years): +0.1 pct to 165.75
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: unchanged at 157.64

"Today was the first time since August 25 that there was excess supply of CPI-linked bonds," said Gidi Halpern of Meitav Investments and Securities. "Investors are taking profits after prices rose an average five percent since the end of August."

"Expectations are that September's CPI will be a low 0.7 percent, against previous estimates of 1.0 percent. If the slowdown in the economy continues, expectations are that the indices will remain low even in the coming months," he said.
September's CPI will be published on October 15.
Prices fell in both in long-term and short-term CPI-linked bonds, he said.
Halpern said the prices of dollar-linked bonds had risen because of a worldwide strengthening of the dollar. The shekel weakened mildly against the dollar in trading on Wednesday.

Tami Diamantstein, a trader at Israel Discount Bank, attributed today's rise in unlinked bonds to the lower inflation expectations, which were causing investors to move out of CPI-linked bonds. Yields on unlinked bonds are between 15 percent and 17 percent.
Diamantstein said the Treasury's new, three-year Shahar unlinked bond, which closed up 0.1 percent today, was trading at 16.7 percent.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
